text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Pablo Neruda was born on 12 July 1904 in the town of Parral in Chile. His father was a railway employee, and his mother, a teacher, died shortly after his birth; he spent his childhood and youth in Temuco. [D]

He used the pen name Pablo Neruda from 1920. The Nobel Prize biography gives his real name as Neftalí Ricardo Reyes Basoalto; the Library of the National Congress of Chile gives his birth name as Ricardo Eliecer Neftalí Reyes Basoalto and records that a court judgment of 28 December 1946 changed it to Pablo Neruda. [D]

Between 1927 and 1935 he held a series of honorary consulships in Burma, Ceylon, Java, Singapore, Buenos Aires, Barcelona and Madrid; in 1945 he was elected a senator of the Republic and joined the Communist Party of Chile. [D]

After the 1970 presidential election he was named Chile's ambassador to France; the Senate approved the appointment on 21 January 1971 and he presented his credentials at the end of that month. He resigned the post in 1972 and returned to Chile in November 1972. [D]

Medical oncology (genitourinary) consultation within two weeks for suspected metastatic prostate cancer: diagnosis, staging, systemic treatment, radiotherapy, bone health and genetic testing. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Prostate Cancer (2026); Advanced Prostate Cancer: AUA/SUO Guideline, first published 2020 and amended 2023 and 2026 (2026) [S]

Diagnosis and staging: multiparametric MRI of the prostate, an MRI-targeted transperineal biopsy at the urology practice, CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis, a bone scan, and PSMA PET/CT. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Prostate Cancer (2026); Advanced Prostate Cancer: AUA/SUO Guideline, first published 2020 and amended 2023 and 2026 (2026); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, prostate cancer and hypertension monographs (2026) [S]

Bone pain: acetaminophen 1000 mg up to three times a day; spinal cord compression warning signs explained in Spanish, with same-day assessment for new leg weakness or numbness, or loss of bladder or bowel control. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Prostate Cancer (2026) [S]

Care in Spanish, his first language: a professional medical interpreter for every major discussion, written plans in Spanish, appointments placed around his morning writing and his official duties. Guideline: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Prostate Cancer (2026) [S]
